name: Ba'athism
summary: Ba'athism is a secular Arab nationalist ideology of unity, freedom and socialism: one Arab state, liberation from foreign domination and an Arab socialism that puts major industry, utilities and land under public control without Marxist materialism. Aflaq treats religion as heritage rather than a basis of law and looks to a revolutionary vanguard party; the party's 1963 congress text goes further toward planning, collective farming and discarding the parliamentary system.
scope: The Aflaqite mainstream and the party's own congress texts: Michel Aflaq's writings (1943-1971), the 1947 constitution as quoted in scholarship, and the Arab Ba'th Socialist Party's Sixth Congress document of 1963, with scholarship on them. The 1963 text leans Marxist and revises the 1947 line on property and parliament, so where Aflaq and the 1963 text differ the answer says so or is left null. It excludes the personalist regimes of Saddam Hussein and Hafez al-Assad.

notes: Evidence is the party's own words (Aflaq 1943-1971, the 1963 congress text, the party's history) and scholarship; no independent record of the party's rule was read, so no answer rests on actions. Earlier answers that rested on Wikipedia summaries and on the French 1947 constitution (which could not be re-opened) were nulled unless the texts read this pass settle them. Themes searched: economy and property, land, planning, unions, democracy and parliament, the vanguard party, army and conscription, religion and secularism, women, imperialism and foreign policy, Palestine, Arab unity, class and Marxism, youth, culture. Three missing statements recorded in the first pass (lending at interest, state-only schooling, landholdings limited to what the owner can farm) rested on the French 1947 constitution, which could not be re-opened, so they are not repeated; two are already in the bank as ban-interest and land-use-tenure. Themes the texts leave silent include healthcare, tax, drugs, abortion, criminal justice, environment, technology, immigration and most social issues. The uncertainty rule is applied by the validator, not argued here.
